# Jira DC hardening — follow-on to e369

## Context

Epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] delivered Jira Server/Data Center support and met its
operator-approved exit bar (run **30964805133**: 62 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed). This epic holds
the DC work discovered BY that delivery which is hardening rather than the feature itself, so no DC
bug is unparented. Operator decision 2026-08-05: let e369 close, harden here.

## What is in scope — all three children CLOSED, all three changes MERGED to main

* [rebar:4a6d-5bbc-44f4-4a56] (bug) — the capability-map channel **reports rather than fails**, so a
  run made before any Software project exists silently writes a WRONG Epic-field contract. Its
  ORIGINAL fix (a pre-run `await_required_fields` gate) was **REFUTED** in triage and the ticket
  re-scoped to post-run validation. **Change 1642 → `f487b62b3c`.**
* [rebar:a3fa-e8d4-f4aa-4b51] (bug) — capability call sites are cast but not runtime-guarded, so a
  non-capable transport fails silently. **Change 1634 → `671fa77c88`.**
* [rebar:f020-0960-2c42-4d61] (task) — the dormant absence-probe port; the operator ruled **DELETE**
  and the deletion is executed. **Change 1645 → `b95c097fd4`.**

## Explicitly NOT in scope

Cloud-surface defects found by DC parity guards ([rebar:6194-...], [rebar:6a74-...],
[rebar:9a46-...]) — real, but Cloud's. The vacuous-guard class ([rebar:8a5e-b88e-0c3e-4544]) and
capability-map trust infrastructure ([rebar:a9bd-6641-e603-42bc]) are on their own tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] 4a6d is fixed per its recorded OPERATOR DECISION (2026-08-12, option (a)): the capability-map
      workflow validates the Epic-field contract AFTER the agent run and marks the report
      UNVERIFIED / fails the job when the run cannot distinguish "the image lacks the Epic fields"
      from "no Software project existed yet". A pre-run `await_required_fields` gate is OUT of
      scope: it is the pre-create call site bug 941b landed to REMOVE and
      `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` bans in terms, and since `main()` creates no project
      before the agent run the wait would deadlock every run. DELIVERED: `customfield_count()` in the shared readiness module — still the single
      source of the field contract, now consulted AFTER the run — plus the pure
      `epic_field_report_problem()` in `main()`'s finally block: `::error::` naming both 941b
      candidate causes, exit 1, verdict in `run_metadata.json`, artifacts still written
- [x] the map run FAILS rather than reports when the contract cannot be established — proven by a
      test that pins a system-only inventory as not-ready on that surface, not merely by
      configuration. DELIVERED: 12 cells in `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py` — system-only
      inventory refused, provisioned accepted, no field read captured refused, a 401 read
      not mistaken for an empty inventory, and two cells driving `main()` on both verdicts
- [x] **AMENDED** — a3fa is fixed: the four capability call sites are RUNTIME-guarded, and the two
      states an operator must act on differently are reported DISTINCTLY through the EXISTING
      bridge audit channel instead of being swallowed by the surrounding `except Exception`.
      Capability ABSENT is a designed skip (INFO log naming capability and site, plus a durable
      `bridge_alerts` record under `outbound-<capability>-capability-absent`); PRESENT-BUT-RAISED
      keeps the existing warning and `comment_errors` capture with the real exception surfaced.
      *This replaces "…fails loudly rather than silently, with a test that pins the loud failure",
      which prescribed the WRONG outcome:* the operator ruling on a3fa (2026-08-12) is
      skip-vs-failure reported DISTINCTLY, not a hard failure on absence — an unimplemented OPT-IN
      capability on a second backend is by design not an error. Pinned by a mutation-checked test:
      deleting the guard operand turns `test_dispatch_links_absent_capability_is_a_designed_skip`
      RED on the ALERT-KIND assertion, not on an incidental `AttributeError`
- [x] **AMENDED (guard shape)** — the guard is `isinstance` PRIMARY with a `hasattr(client, member)`
      fallback, a deliberate in-code-documented divergence from the isinstance-only shape a3fa's
      plan text and ADR-0083 §193-198 specify. Since Python 3.12 (gh-102433) a `@runtime_checkable`
      `isinstance` resolves members with `inspect.getattr_static`, so a transport forwarding via
      `__getattr__` is declared capability-absent and its writes skipped BY DESIGN — reinstating
      this very defect, now blessed as intentional. CI runs 3.11 AND 3.12, so a version bump is no
      alternative. Pinned by `test_proxying_transport_is_capable_and_is_not_skipped` behind a
      `sys.version_info` split; ADR divergence filed as [rebar:5c21-f24a-f7f8-4a55]
- [x] f020 is decided AND EXECUTED, the decision recorded with its reason, including what it does to
      e369 AC5's both-backends claim on `classify_probe_response`. The operator ruled DELETE; change 1645
      removed `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, all three `probe_remote` implementations, `inbound_probe.py`,
      `adapters/jira/probe.py` and `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` (28 files, +73/-1033) after
      proving zero live callers by BOTH a semantic search and a string grep. Effect on e369: `classify_probe_response` is REMOVED from AC5's shared-unit
      list and **e369's AC5 is amended on that ticket to say so**, narrowing the "one shared
      implementation imported by both backends" claim to the field/value maps, the label sanitizer
      and the link-relation vocabulary — a scope reduction, not a regression: no unit was forked per
      adapter. The orphaned `jira.resolved_statuses` / `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config keys
      are a user-visible surface change, deferred to [rebar:549c-032f-6cb0-4258] and parked behind
      the config-read gate's `# read-via:` marker, which expires when that ticket closes
- [x] **AMENDED** — this epic's changes did not regress the live DC harness. *The original wording,
      "the live DC harness is still GREEN end to end after this epic's changes (0 failed cells)",
      inherited from e369's exit bar, is not certifiable as written: the harness was ALREADY red
      before any of this epic's changes landed, for a cause that is not this epic's.* Scheduled run
      **31362329118** (2026-08-10, head `351e13bbda` — BEFORE changes 1642/1634/1645 landed) ended
      **3 failed, 59 passed, 1 xfailed** with the container up cleanly, so it is not a readiness or
      infrastructure abort. Two failures are stale assertions on an `OK:` line commit `c87afedba8`
      stopped emitting on the canonical `sync` route while the pass in fact converged; the third is
      a runner git-lock timeout. Filed as [rebar:9590-34f5-21a8-41fc], linked
      `discovered_from` this epic, which carries the 0-failed re-green bar forward. What IS
      established here: none of the three changes touches any cell in that failure set, and each
      landed `Verified +1` (full CI) plus, for the reconciler change, the mutation check above.
      [operator-attested] — run evidence lives in GitHub Actions, outside the repo snapshot
- [x] no cell is deleted, skipped or `xfail`ed to reach green (the standing operator constraint).
      Held: no live-DC harness cell was deleted, skipped or `xfail`ed by any of the three changes,
      and the run's single `xfail` (`test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips`) is pre-existing, owned
      by 2b16. The three probe-only unit modules deleted by change 1645 are NOT an instance of
      this constraint: they existed solely to exercise the units the operator ruled deleted and went
      with their subject in a pure deletion — no assertion weakened, no failing cell removed

## Testing

    gh workflow run "Live External Integration" --ref main
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 -q; make lint && make typecheck
